skill.name: writing-bots
skill.description: Design Silverback bots that monitor blockchain events, evaluate conditions, and trigger controlled on-chain or off-chain actions.
skill.summary: Build event-driven blockchain bots with Silverback, operational controls, and staged testing.
skill.author: ApeWorX

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting or benign environment variable examples. Confirmed findings cover remote documentation fetches, third-party installation, and bot execution; semantic review also identified irreversible blockchain actions and tolerance of unresolved failures.

remediation.issue: The workflow installs an unpinned tool and can run generated automation on a user-selected network, including mainnet.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation, pin a reviewed Silverback version, default to testnet, and require separate approval before enabling a signer or mainnet.

remediation.issue: The skill permits continued testing when failures remain unexplained.
remediation.suggestion: Require fail-closed behavior and resolve transaction, signer, and state errors before further privileged or funded testing.

content.value_statement: Blockchain event bots require precise triggers, network settings, and safety controls. This skill guides Silverback bot design, project structure, testing, and operation.
actual_capabilities: Translates blockchain automation requirements into Silverback bot designs.
Selects new-block, event-log, cron, or metric-based triggers.
Structures a bot project with documentation, dependencies, and a main module.
Plans on-chain transactions, notifications, backend requests, and service actions.
Recommends metrics, logs, configurable limits, and circuit-breaker conditions.
Provides Silverback installation and network execution commands.
limitations: Requires current Silverback documentation and the uv package tool.
Does not validate smart contract security, protocol economics, or wallet custody.
Generated bots require human review and testnet validation before funded use.
External messaging, social, and backend integrations need separate credentials and configuration.

use_cases.title: Monitor Contract Events
use_cases.description: Design a bot that watches contract logs and sends controlled notifications or backend requests.

use_cases.title: Automate Protocol Operations
use_cases.description: Plan guarded transaction handlers with signer checks, balance limits, and emergency stops.

use_cases.title: Track On-Chain Metrics
use_cases.description: Define derived metrics and trigger actions when volume, balances, or other signals cross thresholds.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Event Bot
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Silverback bot that watches [network] for [contract event] and sends [notification]. Ask for missing requirements before proposing the project.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for one event and one off-chain response.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Testnet Bot
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a Silverback bot for [testnet] that monitors [contract] and records [metric]. Include project files, logging, limits, and circuit-breaker behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate implementation with testnet safety controls.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Action Bot
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Silverback bot that reacts to [trigger] with [off-chain action] and [transaction]. Separate dry-run, testnet, and signer-enabled modes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced automation with multiple integrations and controlled transactions.

prompt_templates.title: Review and Harden a Bot
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Silverback bot for [network]: [requirements or existing design]. Identify failure modes, state assumptions, spending limits, monitoring, and recovery procedures.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert review before signer access or funded deployment.

output_examples.input: Monitor token transfer events on a testnet and alert an operations channel.
output_examples.output: A project plan with an event-log trigger, contract configuration, structured alerts, deduplication, logging, and a testnet verification checklist.

output_examples.input: Submit a maintenance transaction when a liquidity metric falls below a threshold.
output_examples.output: A guarded workflow with metric calculation, dry-run mode, signer checks, transaction limits, circuit-breaker conditions, and operator approval.

output_examples.input: Review an existing bot before enabling it on mainnet.
output_examples.output: A risk review covering contract addresses, network selection, state handling, duplicate events, signer permissions, spending limits, observability, and shutdown procedures.

best_practices: Confirm network, contracts, triggers, actions, and prohibited scenarios before implementation.
Test without a signer, then use testnet before considering funded mainnet operation.
Add explicit limits, idempotency, logs, alerts, and circuit-breaker conditions.
anti_patterns: Do not install packages or run generated bots without explicit user confirmation.
Do not enable a signer before reviewing transaction logic and spending boundaries.
Do not continue privileged testing while failures or state inconsistencies remain unexplained.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It guides the design and implementation of Python bots using the Silverback SDK.

faq.question: Which blockchain events can it handle?
faq.answer: It covers new blocks, contract event logs, scheduled jobs, and metric thresholds.

faq.question: Can it submit transactions?
faq.answer: Yes. Transaction handlers require careful signer controls, limits, testnet validation, and explicit approval.

faq.question: Does it install Silverback automatically?
faq.answer: The source provides an installation command. Users should review and approve package installation before execution.

faq.question: Can it deploy directly to mainnet?
faq.answer: It can target selected networks, but funded mainnet use should follow dry-run and testnet validation.

faq.question: Does it audit smart contracts?
faq.answer: No. It uses contract interfaces but does not replace contract security review or protocol risk analysis.
